metadata.title: PIRLS-2021: Trends in leesprestaties, leesattitude en leesgedrag van tienjarigen uit Nederland

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report describes PIRLS-2021 data collection in the Netherlands using a representative school sample (164 schools drawn; 131 participating) and standardized paper-based test administration. It states that a school weighting procedure was used when drawing the sample, based on five school characteristics (parental education, average education of mothers at school, parents’ country of origin, mother’s length of residence in the Netherlands, and whether parents are in debt restructuring). However, the report does not provide the specific student-level or school-level weight variable name(s) used in the analysis, nor does it describe whether complex survey weights were applied when producing the reported descriptive results and comparisons. Because this is a descriptive PIRLS national report (no ML modeling is performed), the manuscript does not discuss replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife) or any explicit weighting in the analysis stage.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report uses PIRLS reading achievement scales derived via Item Response Theory, and it discusses that each student receives five plausible values for the test score. However, it does not report how plausible values were combined in the analysis (e.g., Rubin’s rules vs averaging) and does not document any missing-data handling strategy for the analytic results. This is a reporting gap for methodological transparency, especially because PIRLS typically involves nontrivial missingness and PV-based estimation.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the PIRLS-2021 Netherlands national sample of grade 6 (group 6) students from participating schools. A representative sample of 164 schools was drawn with school weighting and urbanization considerations; 131 schools participated (including replacement schools) with an overall response rate of 80%. All group 6 students within participating schools were tested; students completed two reading passages (one per session) under a group adaptive design, and their reading proficiency was estimated by IRT based on their responses. The report does not specify additional analytic exclusions beyond the described school participation and the note that a small subset of respondents was tested in the autumn (wave 2) but that the Netherlands is treated as wave 1 for reporting.

data.outcome_summary: This PIRLS-2021 Netherlands national report presents descriptive trends in reading achievement, reading attitude, and reading behavior for grade 6 students. It reports that the average reading achievement score in 2021 was 527, a decline of 18 points from 2016, and that this is approximately equal to the average of the 21 Western comparison countries (531). The report also shows that reading achievement declined for both reading goals and both comprehension processes between 2016 and 2021, and that the distribution across proficiency levels shifted away from middle/high and especially advanced levels. For reading attitude, reading pleasure decreased (mean scale score 8.8 in 2021) while engagement slightly increased (9.2 in 2021) and self-confidence remained roughly stable (9.9 in 2021). For reading behavior, outside-school reading frequency was stable but time spent reading outside school decreased, with the share reading less than 30 minutes per day rising to 63% in 2021. No machine learning models are estimated; therefore, no ML performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/R²) are available.
